analysis:
Both changed files are Swift test files: SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunnerTests.swift and EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift. I found no production source changes in the supplied evidence, and no changes to trust boundaries, cryptography, authorization, or attestation.

LiveRunnerTests (head lines 115-137) adds a test that Runner.engineEnvironment pins the simulated prefill geometry (chunk, step budget, stripe, max partial prefills) over the family default. It also adds an import of MLXLLM. It uses a tiny random-init GPT-OSS model and touches no network, disk, key or consumer data.

EngineV2KVBackendGateTests (patch hunk @@ -710,19 +710,48) updates assertions to the new geometry. A wide plain chunk (EngineV2Factory.widePrefillChunkTokens) replaces the default solo-prefill stripe for the Gemma 4 / GPT-OSS paths. The paged pool's maxPrefillChunk stays at defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens. A new test, widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry, pins that the paged pool is not resized when the wide chunk replaces the stripe. It also checks that SDK env overrides restore the stripe.

The tests protect against a pool or ring undersizing regression, which would be an availability or abort risk, so they are security-positive or neutral.

Remaining integration question: the production change that sets the wide plain chunk default and the pinned env geometry is not in this batch. Reviewers should confirm that max(chunk, stripe) still sizes the windowed rings and KV charges in the production code (T-041/TB-007 availability and memory-bound context). They should also confirm that no prefix-cache gating (SSD donation bounds, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE) is altered by the geometry change. The base_text unit for the gate tests was truncated at line 598, but the changed region lies at lines 713-754, which is beyond the supplied excerpt.
